note: Items from published NHS England and ICB board papers. Each item carries paper URL, page (PDF page of the linked file, or paragraph number for unpaginated web papers and Word documents) and a verbatim quote. Data only; not for publication without review.

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: Board committee updates: Data, Digital and Technology Committee (BM/26/21(Pu))
items.headline: NHS England board committee concerned at pace of NHS Supply Chain modernisation
items.detail: The Data, Digital and Technology Committee reviewed the NHS Supply Chain modernisation programme, noted operational and cyber risks from legacy technology, and will maintain oversight of progress.
items.quote: expressed concern about the pace of implementation and requested further consideration of options to accelerate delivery

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: Board committee updates: Data, Digital and Technology Committee (BM/26/21(Pu))
items.headline: NHS England wants evidence from ambient voice deployments before wider rollout
items.detail: The Committee asked for independent assurance of the Single Patient Record architecture and security, and for deployment evidence on Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) before any wider rollout.
items.quote: further evidence from Ambient Voice Technology deployments on safety, clinician intervention, productivity, patient experience and frontline benefits to inform decisions on wider rollout

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: Board committee updates: New Hospital Programme Board (BM/26/21(Pu))
items.headline: New Hospital Programme: Hospital 2.0 framework secured, 10 contractors for 11 Wave 1 schemes
items.detail: The New Hospital Programme (NHP) Board update says the Hospital 2.0 Alliance framework was secured at the end of July 2026; Wave 1 trusts, Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) and regions are stocktaking towards Outline Business Case submission, with Wave 2 roundtables planned for autumn.
items.quote: the framework secured at the end of July, with 10 contractors due to deliver 11 Wave 1 schemes

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: Board committee updates: New Hospital Programme Board (BM/26/21(Pu))
items.headline: NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care developing streamlined business-case assurance for new hospitals
items.detail: The Board endorsed work with the NHS England and Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Joint Investment Committee to shorten the time to start construction.
items.quote: streamlined business-case assurance approach intended to reduce the time required to start construction

items.board: NHS England
items.page: executive summary (web page, no page numbers)
items.headline: NHS England finance risk raised from 16 to 20
items.detail: The strategic risk on delivering within the NHS funding envelope rose; the paper lists (paragraph 6) a £160m planning gap within system plans and £11.3bn of planned efficiencies across systems, and says the focus is tight financial control.
items.quote: SRR3 (Delivering Objectives Within the NHS Funding Envelope), which has increased from 16 to 20

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: NHS England Estates Strategy sent back for more work
items.detail: The Strategy Committee asked for clearer grip and ownership, better data on estate utilisation, and modelling of how a shift to digital changes the estate.
items.quote: Further work was commissioned to refine the Estates paper.

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: NHS England reviewing market management and patient choice
items.detail: The Strategy Committee discussed challenged healthcare markets and options for commissioning and oversight; further work is to come before Board consideration.
items.quote: how NHS England can support effective commissioning, improve oversight of healthcare markets

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: Board committee updates: Finance and Performance Committee (BM/26/21(Pu))
items.headline: NHS England looking at payment reform to shift funding from acute providers to neighbourhood care
items.detail: The Finance and Performance Committee considered payment mechanisms and incentives for neighbourhood health services and asked for robust modelling before Board consideration.
items.quote: the potential shift of activity and funding from acute providers towards neighbourhood-based care

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: Delays to senior NHS England appointments from new Department of Health and Social Care approvals
items.detail: The People Committee reports that approval requirements introduced in June 2026 restrict pay, senior appointments, promotions and contract extensions, including Regional Director vacancies.
items.quote: delays caused by new Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) approval requirements introduced in June 2026

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: Summary of NHS Genomic Medicine Services Directions 2026 (BM/26/25(Pu))
items.page: executive summary (web page, no page numbers)
items.headline: NHS England directed to build national electronic genomic test ordering system
items.detail: Directions issued on 11 September 2026 require an IT system and data collection for the Genomics Order Management Service, replacing manual paper processes between NHS organisations and laboratories.
items.quote: NHS England is directed to establish an IT system and to collect and analyse data to deliver the Genomics Order Management Service

items.board: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB and NHS Northamptonshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Board papers 15 October 2026 (boards meeting in common in public)
items.headline: Leicestershire, Rutland and Northamptonshire cluster to tender services via the Provider Selection Regime
items.detail: The 2027/28 commissioning intentions say services will go to tender through the Provider Selection Regime (PSR) where benefits are identified, with all existing contracts and activity reviewed and re-commissioned before the end of 2028/29.
items.quote: services will be put up for tender via PSR to encourage partner collaboration

items.board: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB and NHS Northamptonshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Board papers 15 October 2026 (boards meeting in common in public)
items.headline: Third Community Diagnostic Centre planned in both Leicester and Northamptonshire in 2027/28; Northamptonshire elective hub
items.detail: The commissioning intentions say Northamptonshire and Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland (LLR) will each open a third Community Diagnostic Centre (CDC) in 2027/28, and an elective hub is scheduled in Northamptonshire.
items.quote: With both Northants and LLR opening a 3rd CDC in 27/28.

items.board: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB and NHS Northamptonshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Board papers 15 October 2026 (boards meeting in common in public)
items.headline: Leicestershire, Rutland and Northamptonshire cluster needs £21m of in-year mitigations
items.detail: Finance assurance report to the boards in common: a stocktake in early October identified mitigations required to reach a balanced position; month 5 position reported as break-even.
items.quote: A financial stocktake took place in early October to identify mitigations to action in second half of the year

items.board: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB and NHS Northamptonshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Board papers 15 October 2026 (boards meeting in common in public)
items.headline: Leicestershire, Rutland and Northamptonshire cluster reports underperformance on variable drugs and devices
items.detail: The finance report offsets a £19.3m pressure on diagnostic imaging, urgent care and elective activity at University Hospitals of Leicester with underperformance on variable drugs and devices.
items.quote: partially offset by £4.8m of underperformance for variable drugs and devices

items.board: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB and NHS Northamptonshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Board papers 15 October 2026 (boards meeting in common in public)
items.headline: Leicestershire, Rutland and Northamptonshire 2027/28 commissioning intentions include remote monitoring and diabetes technologies
items.detail: The high-level summary lists increased use of digital, AI and remote monitoring and improved access to prevention programmes including diabetes technologies, plus virtual wards and Hospital at Home.
items.quote: Increase use of digital, AI and remote monitoring

items.board: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB and NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (boards in common)
items.headline: Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin and Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent to set up a Procurement Oversight Group
items.detail: The Joint Strategic Transformation and Commissioning Committee approved subgroup terms of reference and noted a Procurement Oversight Group will be established, its terms of reference still in development.
items.quote: A Procurement Oversight Group will also be established, with terms of reference currently in development.

items.board: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB and NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (boards in common)
items.headline: New Efficiency Oversight Group across both ICBs
items.detail: The group will oversee delivery of agreed efficiency schemes, track against Medium-Term Financial Plan targets and identify new opportunities for the pipeline, reporting through a Gateway Process.
items.quote: newly established operational group across Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB and Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB cluster arrangements

items.board: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB and NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (boards in common)
items.headline: County Hospital Urgent Treatment Centre revenue business case approved
items.detail: The Committee approved the revenue business case for the County Urgent Treatment Centre (UTC) after capital was approved through left shift funding, subject to a discussion on overheads.
items.quote: approved the UHNM County UTC revenue Business Case subject to a further financial discussion on overheads

items.board: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB and NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (boards in common)
items.headline: Diabetic wellness kit evaluation presented to both boards
items.detail: Presented as a resident story, the MyHealthKits evaluation across 13 general practices says it estimated cost reductions from lower reported healthcare use, and sets out recommendations for wider rollout.
items.quote: the evaluation estimated a total cost reduction of £36,863 over 12 weeks, equal to £288 per patient

items.board: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB and NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (meetings in common)
items.paperTitle: ICB Board papers, agenda items 1 to 14
items.headline: Lincolnshire fourth Community Diagnostic Centre in Boston ahead of schedule, completion expected March 2027
items.detail: The programme overview says Lincolnshire diagnostic waits are worsening and capacity is being added through the Boston centre.
items.quote: the fourth CDC in Boston continues to progress positively, remaining within budget and approximately six weeks ahead of schedule

items.board: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB and NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (meetings in common)
items.paperTitle: ICB Board papers, agenda items 1 to 14
items.headline: Lincolnshire, Derbyshire and Nottinghamshire using mobile MRI and insourcing to cut diagnostic waits
items.detail: Lincolnshire reports 50.5% of patients waiting more than six weeks for a diagnostic test against a plan of 37.0%; the commissioner response includes temporary capacity.
items.quote: use of mobile MRI, insourcing and additional sessions

items.board: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB and NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (meetings in common)
items.paperTitle: ICB Board papers, agenda items 1 to 14
items.headline: Derbyshire, Lincolnshire and Nottinghamshire efficiency increasingly reliant on one-off measures
items.detail: The finance report says the ICBs forecast achieving a £163.1m efficiency target but recurrent efficiencies are below plan, offset by one-off benefits.
items.quote: delivery remains increasingly dependent upon non-recurrent measures

items.board: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB and NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (meetings in common)
items.paperTitle: ICB Board papers, agenda items 1 to 14
items.headline: Lincolnshire stoma, trans-anal irrigation and catheter care survey finds reviews are a gap
items.detail: A countywide survey (176 responses) found home delivery of equipment widely used and working well, but many people never reviewed; findings shared with Medicines Optimisation to inform service improvement.
items.quote: Regular reviews were a key gap, with many people reporting they had never received a review.

items.board: NHS South Yorkshire ICB
items.headline: South Yorkshire: NHS England has withheld second-quarter deficit support funding
items.detail: Month 4 finance report: Quarter 2 deficit support funding (DSF) is not agreed pending de-risking of the efficiency programme, now forecast at 83.6% (£100.0m of £119.5m target).
items.quote: Quarter 2 funding has been withheld by NHS England pending further assurance on the delivery of the ICBs efficiency programme

items.board: NHS South Yorkshire ICB
items.headline: South Yorkshire forms a fortnightly Investment Prioritisation Panel
items.detail: Part of the turnaround measures, alongside strict grip and control on discretionary spend and slippage.
items.quote: Formation of a fortnightly Investment Prioritisation Panel to review proposed recurrent and new investments across the ICB

items.board: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB and NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Agenda item 12: Financial Plan and Delivery, Month 4
items.headline: Herefordshire/Worcestershire and Coventry/Warwickshire set up £10.5m neighbourhood health left-shift fund
items.detail: Split by place: Warwickshire £3.0m, Coventry £3.0m, Worcestershire £3.0m, Herefordshire £1.5m, aimed at shifting activity from hospital to community and preventative services.
items.quote: established a Neighbourhood Health Investment (Left Shift) fund of £10.5m

items.board: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB and NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (boards in common)
items.paperTitle: Agenda item 12: Financial Plan and Delivery, Month 4
items.headline: Herefordshire/Worcestershire and Coventry/Warwickshire financial framework moves towards outcome-based contracts
items.detail: One of six principles agreed with system partners in May 2026, with a joint medium term plan and contracting and payment reform workstreams to follow.
items.quote: Correct the financial imbalance by moving to outcome-based contracts.

items.board: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB and NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (boards in common)
items.headline: Herefordshire/Worcestershire and Coventry/Warwickshire to expect peri-operative optimisation schemes in future commissioning intentions
items.detail: The paper lists one-stop peri-operative assessment clinics, care co-ordinators, digitally supported prehabilitation, tobacco, alcohol and dietetic support, intravenous or oral iron pathways and medicines optimisation.
items.quote: Schemes that support this model, which will be expected as part of future commissioning intentions

items.board: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB and NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (boards in common)
items.headline: Additional mobile breast screening unit secured at UHCW until March 2027
items.detail: The spotlight paper says the extra mobile unit shortens the screening round to six months, principally in Coventry.
items.quote: An additional mobile unit has been secured at UHCW until March 2027 to shorten the screening round to six months

items.board: NHS Gloucestershire ICB (joint cluster board with NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB)
items.headline: Gloucestershire and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire merger planning assumes April 2027
items.detail: The Joint Transition Committee reported six workstreams and an oversight group established, with due diligence structure; the paper refers to a merger programme without naming the bodies in that paragraph.
items.quote: against the working assumption of implementation from April 2027

items.board: NHS Gloucestershire ICB and NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB (joint cluster board)
items.paperTitle: Agenda item 6: Month 5 (August) Cluster Finance Report
items.headline: Gloucestershire efficiency slippage from slower dapagliflozin switching
items.detail: Forecast efficiency delivery is £53.5m, £0.6m below plan, driven by slower uptake of dapagliflozin switching.
items.quote: Slower uptake at the start of the year on Dapagliflozin switching being the main driver of the slippage.

items.board: NHS Gloucestershire ICB and NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB (joint cluster board)
items.paperTitle: Agenda item 6: Month 5 (August) Cluster Finance Report
items.headline: Gloucestershire prescribing overspend driven by generic drug price concessions
items.detail: Primary care prescribing forecasts a £5m overspend; the paper cites an average of 234 concessions per month April to August, and the BNSSG prescribing forecast overspend is £2m.
items.quote: exceptionally high generic drug price concessions

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: NHS England Strategic Risk Register: Board summaries (Annex A to risk report, October 2026)
items.headline: NHS England says 45% of NHS estates infrastructure is not fit for current services
items.detail: The strategic risk on capital and estates, scored 20, now covers estates sustainability and estates workforce capability as well as capital. The risk owner notes a national asset survey is being mobilised and ICS (Integrated Care System) estate strategies are complete.
items.quote: 45% of estates infrastructure is not fit for the services the NHS delivers today

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: NHS England Strategic Risk Register: Board summaries (Annex A to risk report, October 2026)
items.headline: NHS England keeps national supply chain fragility at the joint highest score, 20, citing procurement reform
items.detail: The supply chain risk covers medicines, medical products and non-clinical goods and services. Mitigations named include supply chain diversification, domestic manufacturing, improved visibility of shortages and enhanced supplier reporting.
items.quote: Progress is being made through domestic manufacturing initiatives, procurement reform and broader resilience programmes.

items.board: NHS England
items.paperTitle: NHS England Operational Risk Register: Quarter 2 summaries (Annex B to risk report, October 2026)
items.headline: NHS England pandemic preparedness risk includes medical devices stockpiling
items.detail: The operational risk on pandemic preparedness lists assured critical care, PPE (personal protective equipment) and medical devices stockpiling and deployment among its controls, and says the Department of Health and Social Care has taken formal accountability for medtech pandemic preparedness.
items.quote: Operational resilience is being strengthened through assured critical care, PPE and medical devices stockpiling and deployment arrangements

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: NHS England: over half of £8.3bn provider efficiencies assessed as high risk at month 4
items.detail: The month 4 finance section lists delivery of provider efficiencies as a principal risk to the 2026/27 financial position, alongside a remaining planning gap of about 160 million pounds.
items.quote: Delivery of £8.3bn of provider efficiencies, over half of which are assessed as high risk.

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: NHS England forecasts 176 million pounds national capital underspend at month 4
items.detail: Providers had spent 1,176 million pounds on capital schemes to month 4, 12% of full-year budget, against a Department of Health and Social Care provider and commissioning capital budget of 10,709 million pounds for 2026/27.
items.quote: we are currently forecasting an underspend of £176m.

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: NHS England orders Community Diagnostic Centres and low-utilisation scanners to hit 2026/27 activity plans
items.detail: Diagnostic waits over six weeks were 23.1% in July 2026, 1.3 percentage points worse than July 2025. Actions include managing trusts with low utilisation of CT, MRI, non-obstetric ultrasound, echocardiography and endoscopy, and 45 trusts must eliminate six-month colonoscopy waits by September 2026.
items.quote: All CDCs must deliver to their 2026/27 activity plans

items.board: NHS England
items.headline: NHS England holds back Deficit Support Funding from thirteen organisations at Quarter 2
items.detail: The total held back at month 4 is 19 million pounds. The report puts the year-to-date overspend at 194 million pounds, driven by industrial action and shortfall in efficiency delivery, with bank spend emerging as a significant overspend.
items.quote: Thirteen organisations have had their Deficit Support Funding (DSF) held back at Quarter 2

items.board: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board
items.headline: South East ICBs get assurance on shared procurement, people, clinical policy and digital services transition
items.detail: A South East ICBs' Chief Executives Joint Committee met on 11 August 2026. It noted progress on the Office of Pan-ICB Commissioning ahead of further delegated commissioning from April 2027, and an interim two-year data centre hosting arrangement for digital infrastructure.
items.quote: received assurance on the transition of procurement, people services, clinical policy and digital services

items.board: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Surrey and Sussex consults on a digital, data and intelligence shared service it would host for South East ICBs
items.detail: A structural consultation is under way for a new digital, data and intelligence service with partners across the South East region.
items.quote: This will be a shared service that NHS Surrey and Sussex will host on behalf of others.

items.board: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Surrey and Sussex 166.1 million pound efficiency programme on plan, with 11.6 million pounds non-recurrent
items.detail: 55.4 million pounds was delivered at month 4. Remaining medium-risk schemes total 23.0 million pounds and relate primarily to continuing healthcare.
items.quote: £11.6m of delivery is currently non-recurrent and will require a recurrent solution in future years.

items.board: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Surrey and Sussex capital plan is 18.6 million pounds, weighted to the second half
items.detail: The plan splits 9.1 million pounds for primary care and 9.5 million pounds for strategic capital investment; delivery depends on securing remaining scheme approvals.
items.quote: capital plan is £18.6m, comprising £9.1m for primary care and £9.5m for strategic capital investment

items.board: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Surrey and Sussex commissioning principles favour procurement that encourages market innovation
items.detail: The five-year plan (page 12 of the paper) also says the ICB may delegate commissioning, commission across wider geographies, and consider decommissioning services where value cannot be shown.
items.quote: We will adopt procurement approaches which encourage the provider market to innovate, giving our residents access to leading-edge technology and services.

items.board: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Lancashire and South Cumbria proposes a single vascular network and one arterial centre at Royal Preston Hospital, public consultation from October 2026
items.detail: About 650 inpatient cases a year would transfer; around 2 million pounds of capital is needed, funded from provider trust capital plans; projected 1.8 million pounds annual system-wide improvement. Decision-making business case due Q3 2026/27, final decision by Q4 2026/27.
items.quote: an eight-week public consultation is planned from Oct-2026

items.board: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Lancashire and South Cumbria caps high-cost drugs and devices spend with its four acute trusts, with risk and gainshare
items.detail: High-cost drugs and devices delayed contract sign-off; a capped approach has been agreed with the four main acute providers, with further work needed to maximise value in future years.
items.quote: expenditure to be capped at a maximum level and a risk/gainshare agreement to be varied into the contracts once finalised

items.board: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Lancashire and South Cumbria needs about 214.6 million pounds of cost mitigations in 2026/27
items.detail: The plan leads to a 34.9 million pound deficit under the NHS England control total, with deficit support funding. Mitigations are Waste Reduction Plan about 127 million, organisational change about 36 million and other about 52 million pounds.
items.quote: requires a minimum delivery of c.£214.6m cost mitigations

items.board: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Lancashire and South Cumbria confirms Andy Knox and Andy Curran as substantive co-medical directors
items.detail: Both had been acting; Andy Knox is a GP and Andy Curran a consultant in emergency medicine at the Preston major trauma centre.
items.quote: Andy Knox and Andy Curran were appointed as the substantive

items.board: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: Board Assurance Report: Finance Committee - 28 July 2026 (item 14)
items.headline: Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB finance committee alerted to risk of Commissioning Support Unit (CSU) digital services overspend
items.detail: Risk arises during the transition from the current South Central and West CSU arrangements.
items.quote: risk of significant Commissioning Support Unit overspend on Digital Services during the transition

items.board: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: Board Assurance Report: Finance Committee - 28 July 2026 (item 14)
items.headline: Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB Spending Control Group remains in place; two contracts over £2m reviewed
items.detail: Committee assured the Spending Control Group stays to maintain financial grip and control; full-year 2026/27 plan is breakeven.
items.quote: two significant contracts, greater than £2m, had been taken to Spending Control Group since the previous meeting

items.board: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: Board Assurance Report: Finance Committee - 25 June 2026 (item 14)
items.headline: Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB receives Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27
items.detail: Plan sets out how the capital elements the ICB directly influences are allocated and what capital spending will enable; due at the private Board on 1 July 2026.
items.quote: The Committee received the Joint Capital Resource Use Plan for 2026/27

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: West Yorkshire plans £437.9m of capital in 2026/27, including £16.8m on CT and MRI replacement
items.detail: Total West Yorkshire capital plan with national programme breakdown; Return to Constitutional Standards capital includes £16.8m diagnostics (CT/MRI replacement plus physiological science equipment), £18.7m elective surgical hub expansion in Leeds and £25.4m urgent and emergency care. Also £12.3m digital infrastructure (electronic health records, end user modernisation, digital diagnostic capability).
items.quote: The total West Yorkshire capital plan for 2026/27 is £437.9m

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: West Yorkshire diagnostics capital focuses on replacing CT and MRI equipment
items.detail: The Return to Constitutional Standards (national elective, cancer and diagnostic access standards) capital schemes include diagnostics, an elective surgical hub expansion and two Same Day Emergency Care units.
items.quote: £16.8m of Diagnostics expenditure focusing on replacing CT/MRI equipment

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: West Yorkshire operational capital goes mainly on end-of-life medical equipment, maintenance and IT
items.detail: Provider operational capital allocation for 2026/27 is £153.4m (plan £160.9m with over-programming). Also £32.6m additional Estates Safety funding for backlog maintenance.
items.quote: Operational capital expenditure plans predominantly relate to the replacement of medical equipment that is at the end of its life

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: Leeds Teaching Hospitals leading £21m centralised aseptic pharmacy hub, construction partner procured
items.detail: WYAAT aseptic pharmacy hub (abbreviation as printed in the paper); design work being finalised.
items.quote: The construction partner has been procured, and design work is being finalised.

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: Leeds new hospital delayed; Leeds Teaching Hospitals backlog maintenance risk rises
items.detail: Paper states recent decisions delayed the build date for the new Leeds hospital, with new plans being devised to keep current hospitals running until a new hospital is built between 2035 and 2040.
items.quote: Recent decisions have delayed the build date for the new hospital

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: Bradford District Care Trust Lynfield Mount £65m redevelopment adds 10 acute adult beds by 2028/29
items.detail: Full Business Case approved in January 2026.
items.quote: The Full Business Case was approved in January 2026 for a £65m investment due to complete in 2028/29

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: Airedale RAAC programme £24.6m planned in 2026/27; new hospital enabling works up to £45m
items.detail: Airedale (Reinforced Autoclaved Aerated Concrete, RAAC) programme planned spend £24.6m in 2026/27; new hospital enabling works up to £45m (page 11); electronic patient record capital about £8m (page 12).
items.quote: Planned expenditure in 2026/27 is £24.6m, which enable the rolling programme of ward works, inspection and management regime and roof works.

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.paperTitle: West Yorkshire Joint Capital Resource Use Plan 2026/27 (item 18)
items.headline: Mid Yorkshire Teaching Hospitals electronic patient record: £18m investment approved
items.detail: Full Business Case approved in 2025/26, two-tranche implementation.
items.quote: The Full Business Case was approved 2025/26 for an £18m investment

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.headline: West Yorkshire ICB cuts establishment from 1,158 to 691 whole-time equivalent posts
items.detail: Running-cost reduction following two voluntary redundancy schemes; new structure implementation began 1 September 2026; 91 colleagues not yet in a role.
items.quote: The number of posts in the ICB establishment has reduced from 1,158 to 691 whole-time equivalents, a reduction of 40%.

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.headline: West Yorkshire ICB recruiting a new Executive Director of Finance; new Executive Director of Nursing appointed
items.detail: Julie Clennell appointed Executive Director of Nursing; recruitment for Finance Director under way.
items.quote: Recruitment to appoint a new Executive Director of Finance is underway.

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.headline: West Yorkshire proposes four Neighbourhood Health Centre schemes for national support, two seeking Public Private Partnership funding
items.detail: Pipeline of 38 schemes; Huddersfield National Health Innovation Campus and Castleford Health Centre request Public Private Partnership funding; national decision expected in coming months.
items.quote: two are significant NHC schemes requesting Public Private Partnership funding

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Mid Yorkshire Teaching Hospitals MRI capacity constraints mitigated with mobile scanners
items.detail: Longer than six-week diagnostic waits at Mid Yorkshire Teaching NHS Trust (MYTT) linked to Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) capacity.
items.quote: Mobile MRI scanners are mitigating this pressure

items.board: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board
items.headline: West Yorkshire NHS system ended 2025/26 in deficit although the ICB posted a surplus
items.detail: ICB £21.4m surplus against £15.4m plan; provider deficits outweighed it.
items.quote: the wider West Yorkshire NHS system did not achieve break-even reporting an overall deficit

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: North East and North Cumbria ICB forecasts £121.1m of efficiencies in 2026/27, in line with plan
items.detail: At month 4, £43.4m delivered year to date; All-Age Continuing Care (AACC) efficiency delivery is a growing risk; net unmitigated risk reduced to £15.6m.
items.quote: forecasting delivery of £121.1m of efficiencies for the year in line with plan

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: NENC ICB to host specialised commissioning for four North East and Yorkshire ICBs from April 2027, subject to legislation
items.detail: Transfer of specialised commissioning to ICBs planned from April 2027; shadow joint committee across the four ICBs starts in October.
items.quote: with North East and North Cumbria ICB agreed as the host organisation on behalf of the four North East and Yorkshire ICBs

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: Commissioning Support Units to close in March 2027; NENC ICB managing transition of North of England Commissioning Support services including GP IT and corporate IT
items.detail: Transition of North of England Commissioning Support (NECS) services including GP IT and corporate IT; programme assurance rated amber.
items.quote: ahead of the planned closure of Commissioning Support Units in March 2027

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: NENC ICB signals more directive commissioning from 2027/28 as demand outpaces funded activity
items.detail: Demand up about 4.6% at month 4 against 3% activity growth despite 5.7% funded growth in elective activity.
items.quote: a more targeted and directive approach to commissioning in 2027/28

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: NENC ICB preparing digital procurement for all-age continuing care
items.detail: Progress report says digital procurement preparation and data assurance for All-Age Continuing Care are progressing.
items.quote: Digital procurement preparation and improved AACC data assurance are progressing

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: NENC ICB began rolling out an ADHD referral management service in late June 2026
items.detail: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder referral management service, part of a new ICB Commissioning Policy for ADHD and autism pathways.
items.quote: The roll out of the ADHD referral management service began in late June 2026

items.board: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
items.headline: NENC ICB exploring system control totals for referral to treatment with regional team
items.detail: Paper also says breast-service recovery depends on radiology workforce capacity.
items.quote: The ICB is exploring a potential model of system control totals for RTT with the NEY regional team.

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: Birmingham and Solihull and Black Country cluster taking legal advice on route for physical health anchor contracts
items.detail: Cluster Board paper says the service line scope for the physical health anchor contracts is being finalised with designate trusts. Stage 1 gateway submissions for the mental health and learning disability anchor arrangement were received on 1 September.
items.quote: legal advice is being taken on whether award should proceed through a Provider Selection Regime

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: Business case proposes 24/7 single point of access, urgent community response and expanded virtual wards across Birmingham and the Black Country
items.detail: The business case, co-created by University Hospitals Birmingham and Birmingham Community Healthcare, is under financial and impact scrutiny. Walsall and Wolverhampton single point of access goes live on 1 October and Dudley and Sandwell on 1 November.
items.quote: proposes a 24/7 single point of access alongside 24/7 urgent community response and expanded virtual ward capacity

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: Birmingham urgent treatment centre and out-of-hours redesign: independent options review then public Board decision planned for November
items.detail: Response to Birmingham Health and Adult Social Care Committee feedback due 17 September; independent options review led by Olovus on 24 September.
items.quote: an independent options review led by Olovus on 24 September and the public Board decision planned for November

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: Both ICBs forecast break-even; 90% of 2027/28 efficiencies identified, with Right to Choose and medicines price concessions flagged as pressures
items.detail: Paper lists ADHD and autism Right to Choose activity, medicines price concessions and all-age continuing healthcare as continuing pressures. Final financial framework products for Place and anchor contract holders expected before Christmas.
items.quote: the medium-term plan continues to show break-even across the period with 90% of 2027/28 efficiencies identified

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: Endoscopy and glaucoma backlogs being tackled through community optometry and community diagnostics
items.detail: Paper refers to endoscopy waits at University Hospitals Birmingham and the glaucoma follow-up backlog at Royal Wolverhampton Hospital.
items.quote: being addressed in part through community optometry and community diagnostics

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: NHS England approved redundancy business cases for the Birmingham and Solihull and Black Country ICB cluster on 21 August
items.detail: Formal notices and settlements issued from 1 September; the paper says the transition is in all material respects complete.
items.quote: NHS England approved the phase one compulsory redundancy and phase two voluntary redundancy business cases on 21 August

items.board: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board and NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board (Joint ICB Cluster Board)
items.headline: Winter Plan 2026/27 leaves a residual gap of 77 general and acute beds after mitigations
items.detail: Modelling shows a peak deficit of 412 general and acute beds; planned mitigations cover 335. The Board was asked to delegate final sign-off to the Chair and Chief Executive; plan due to NHS England by 30 September 2026.
items.quote: leaving a residual gap of 77 beds where further mitigation is required

items.board: NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board

items.quote: The 2026-27 Primary Care Prescribing Cost Improvement Plan is targeting £14.5m of savings

items.board: NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board

items.board: NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board

items.detail: Paper put to the Board for approval. The review would cover quality, safety, outcomes, inequalities, workforce, service configuration and commissioning arrangements.
items.quote: It is therefore proposed that NHS Thames Valley undertake a comprehensive system-wide review of maternity and neonatal services.

items.quote: the total number of unpaid invoices was now down to 13175
